sections.changelog:
Added

  • `include` shortcode attribute: `[mvweb-cp id="10" include="31,12,27"]` shows only the listed child pages, in the order the ids are written. It is what a hub page split into thematic groups needs — one shortcode per group under its own heading — and it arranges a group without touching the Order field of every page. The counterpart to `exclude`, which the shortcode has always had
  • Editors get their own diagnostic when an `include` list matches nothing: «none of the pages listed is a published child page of page N», instead of the message about a parent with no children. A value that parses to no id at all (`include="none"`) lands there too, rather than quietly falling back to the full list of children

Fixed

  • WordPress 6.7+ no longer reports «translation loading for the mvweb-child-pages domain was triggered too early» on every request. The warning came from the hub, not from this plugin's own strings: `MVweb_Menu` loaded its catalogue from its constructor, which runs on `plugins_loaded`, and that catalogue asks every installed plugin to register itself — those callbacks translate their own labels, so every MVweb domain was pulled in before `init`. The hub now loads it on `init` (a plugin activated later still gets it straight away), and this plugin's own `load_plugin_textdomain()` moved to `init` as well. Shared class bumped to 2.6.2 so the fixed copy wins the newest-wins loader; the other plugins pick it up at their next release

Notes

  • `include` filters the children the query already returned rather than going into `get_pages()`: the list stays a list of the given parent's children (an id from another branch is not there to be picked), `exclude` keeps working next to it, and several group shortcodes on one page share a single database query. Passing the ids to `get_pages()` would have done none of that — the core drops `post__not_in`, `child_of` and `parent` as soon as `include` is set
  • `orderby` and `order` are ignored alongside `include`, which carries the order itself; `limit` still cuts the tail of the list
